An open-source ADE that works like a messaging app. Chat with the AI agents on your computer, from desktop or phone. Built for developers and everyday people. 

 
 Codex · Claude Code · Kimi Code · DeepSeek Harness · Antigravity · Pi · oh-my-pi (omp)

 57-second product overview · YouTube · Animated overview 

TaroBird is an open-source, self-hosted ADE (agentic development environment) that works like a messaging app, built for developers and everyday people alike. It brings command-line agents such as Codex and Claude Code, running on your computers or servers, into a single conversation interface: assign tasks, answer questions, follow each run and receive deliverables from desktop or phone. Bots, conversations and files stay on your own hosts.

 
 
 Native engines Runs the official CLIs and keeps each engine's native agent capabilities. 
 Desktop and phone macOS, Windows and mobile share the same Bots and conversations, so work continues anywhere. 
 Multi-host network Each computer joins your private network with its own Bots. 
 
 
 Groups and collaboration Multi-Bot groups with topics, plus visual workflows with Agent Bus. 
 Cross-host tasks Bots hand tasks, files and results to one another across hosts. 
 ADHD mode Up to 12 desktop conversations side by side, each moving independently. 
 
 

 Desktop 
 macOS · Windows Organize work by Bot or by conversation, inspect each run, and review replies and files. 

 
 
 

 Mobile 
 Start on your computer. Continue on your phone. Read replies, answer questions and receive files in the same conversations. 

 
 
 
 Full-size inbox · Full-size chat 

 
 ADHD · Parallel conversation workspace 
 Keep several Bot conversations in view, each moving independently. Switch to ADHD beside Bots / Chats, then select the chats for your board. 

 
 
 
 Desktop only · macOS / Windows · Recorded from the real interface with demonstration data · Full-size view 

- Work in parallel. Select up to 12 chats across hosts. Each pane keeps its own messages, draft and input; removing a pane neither closes the conversation nor stops its running task.
- Flexible layout. Use automatic layout or 2–6 columns, resize the sidebar, reorder panes or expand one to focus. ADHD text size is adjustable from 11 to 16 px.
- Actions in place. Questions, replies and files stay in their own conversations, and the board layout is saved on this device.

 
 Agent Bus · Visual multi-Bot collaboration 
 Assign a task to each step and see how work moves between Bots. Open a saved Bus from the sidebar to view member conversations alongside the workflow. 

 
 
 
 Desktop only · macOS / Windows · Real interface with demonstration data and a simulated run status · Full-size workflow · Member configuration 

- Orchestrate the workflow. Choose delegation, parallel work, sequential steps, verification or a research crew, and bind each step to a Bot and a result conversation with its own task.
- Progress at a glance. The flow shows the status of every step while the panes show its output. Saved Buses are reusable, and closing the panel does not stop a running collaboration.
- Runs within one host. Members work in independent sessions and record their results in the bound conversations. Design and operation · Per-step tasks

 Actual UI with demonstration data · Screenshot provenance · ADHD design and verification 

 
 Groups and topics · Bring your Bots into one conversation 
 Put research, writing and review Bots in one group to work through the same question. Join the group from desktop or phone, and organize each project or question into its own topic. 

 
 
 
 Actual UI with demonstration data; replies are illustrative, not model execution · Group members currently belong to one host · Discussion settings · Group guide 

- Choose who replies. In ordinary group chat, select or @ the Bots you want to answer. Switch to parallel replies for everyone to answer independently.
- Keep topics separate. Create topics within the group for different projects or questions. Topics use the same group members and keep their own conversation history.
- Choose a discussion mode. Use group chat, parallel replies, roundtable or independent review. Automatic discussions support speaking order and round limits, with controls to pause, resume or end a discussion.

 
 Connected Bots · One team across your computers 
 Give one Bot a goal. Let authorized Bots on other computers contribute their part. Tasks, files and results travel between Bots; each machine runs its own work. 

 
 
 
 Illustrative messaging pattern, not a live run · Each task direction needs permission 

 “Ask the Windows Bot to build and test this change, and the server Bot to analyze the data. Bring their reports and files back here.”

- One Bot can coordinate several machines. In one task, tell a Bot which parts to send to which hosts. It acts as your point of contact, collects those replies and combines the results. Each receiving Bot works through its own engine and permissions on its host.
- Peers can help one another. A review Bot can ask a research Bot for context, or a coding Bot can hand a change to a test Bot. The same message flow works within one host and across hosts; a central Bot is optional.
- Bring another computer's Bots into the team. Connect the joining computer to an existing host, then confirm joining under Settings → Network & connections → My network . Authorized desktop and phone clients can access its Bots. Hosts must be online and mutually reachable for a handoff.
- Keep the work traceable. Dedicated collaboration conversations retain tasks and replies, and the recipient sees the source host and Bot. Files you hand off are copied to the receiving host; joining a network does not merge workspaces or gran

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
01 · Install the host
Install TaroBird on your computer, make it a host and create a Bot.		 02 · Pair your phone
Scan the QR code on your phone, then approve its 8-digit code.		 03 · Connect from anywhere
Reach your Bots over Tailscale or a VPS relay.
01 · Install the host
  1. Install the desktop App. On macOS, drag TaroBird.app into Applications; the App is notarized by Apple. On Windows, run the installer. The installer is not yet code-signed, so if SmartScreen appears, choose More info → Run anyway. Existing Mac users should use Settings → General → App updates to keep their current installation location; do not keep both TaroBot.app and TaroBird.app. For a manual upgrade, follow the rename transition.
  2. On first launch, choose Use this computer as a host and name the computer.
  3. Create a Bot with an engine installed on this computer.
02 · Pair your phone
  1. Install TaroBird on your phone. iOS: download the stable app from the App Store, or install Apple’s TestFlight app and join the public beta. App Store availability varies by country or region; TaroBird is not currently listed in mainland China. Android: use the APK from Releases.
  2. On the computer, open Settings → Network & connections → Add device, choose a connection option and generate the QR code. The host restarts briefly the first time, so let current tasks finish first.
  3. On the phone, open TaroBird and tap Scan connection QR code, or use Import a QR image or Paste connection details.
  4. The phone displays an 8-digit pairing code, valid for 5 minutes. Enter it on the computer and click Approve pairing; the phone then opens your chats automatically.
03 · Connect from anywhere

Connection options

Each row is a different route to the same computer running your Bots.

  style relay fill:transparent,stroke:#b6bab7,rx:8,ry:8
Option Best for What you need
Local network (LAN) Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi or reachable local network No extra network service; devices must be able to reach each other
Remote access with Tailscale Away from home, with Tailscale on both devices Both devices in the same Tailscale network; no VPS of your own required
VPS relay Away from home, with no VPN on the phone A cloud server (several computers can share one); we recommend letting an AI deploy it

[!TIP] Let your own agent set up the VPS relay. Give Codex, Claude Code or another agent the ready-to-use setup instructions, and ask it to follow the project documentation to deploy and verify the relay. The agent needs terminal access on your host computer and authorized SSH access to your VPS.

With every option above, Bots run on your computer, and chats, files and sign-ins stay there, so keep the computer on and online. The VPS relay only forwards connections; it does not run your Bots. To keep Bots working while the computer is off, see running a full host on a VPS.

Option 1 · Tailscale

  1. Install Tailscale on the computer and the phone, sign in, and join the same Tailscale network.
  2. On the computer, open Settings → Network & connections → Add device, choose Remote access with Tailscale and click Generate Tailscale QR code. TaroBird detects the computer's Tailscale address automatically.
  3. Scan and approve as in Pair your phone. A phone that is already paired can open Me → Connection status & routes and tap Scan a code to update connection to add the Tailscale route without pairing again.

Keep Tailscale connected on both devices, and make sure your Tailscale access rules allow the phone to reach the computer.

Option 2 · VPS relay (recommended: let an AI deploy it)

  1. On the computer, open an AI agent that can use a terminal and SSH, such as Codex or Claude Code. Give it the complete setup prompt together with the VPS SSH alias and the path to your private key (never the key itself). It deploys the relay, issues certificates with automatic renewal, verifies the connection end to end and returns an HTTPS address. To deploy it yourself, follow the manual guide.
  2. On the computer, open Settings → Network & connections → Connection status & routes. Under VPS relays for this host, click Add VPS relay, enter the address and click Verify and save relays.
  3. If an already paired phone does not receive the new route automatically, open Me → Connection status & routes → Edit routes → Add VPS relay address, enter the same address and tap Save routes. A new phone can scan the computer's QR code with VPS relay selected.
  4. Turn off the phone's Wi-Fi and confirm that it connects over cellular data.

Several computers on one VPS: all computers share one relay process and one tunnel port, and each computer takes only one more port for its phones. When you set up the next computer, tell the agent that the VPS already runs a relay and ask it to add the new computer; the existing computers keep their addresses and configuration. Steps

Add more computers

Install TaroBird on the new computer, choose Connect to an existing host, then scan or paste the connection details from Add device on a paired device. On any paired phone or computer, open Devices & network → Enter code to confirm and enter the 8-digit code shown on the new computer; there is no need to be at the host. If the new computer will run its own Bots, confirm joining the network when prompted. Private network

For a host without a desktop window, use the TaroBird CLI. On first launch, macOS may ask for keychain access; choose Always Allow (why).
